newsitem.title: HONG KONG: No holiday for Hong Kong air cargo sector.
newsitem.headline: No holiday for Hong Kong air cargo sector.

text.p: Hong Kong is starting its five day long handover celebrations but for many of the territory's freight forwarders it will be no holiday, industry sources told Reuters.

Some forwarders have been busy clearing shipments before the territory comes to an expected standstill, others report business as usual with the handover having little effect. Many airlines have cancelled flights or revised schedules because goods from their major market will stop being trucked across the border when China has its official handover holiday on July 1.
Air freight is also still due to arrive in the territory from around the world during the holiday and freight forwarding firms are staying open to avoid backlogs when it is all over.
July 3 is expected to be exceptionally busy clearing any backlogs and some industry spokesmen said it might take until July 7 before normal trading patterns are resumed.

Like many firms, DHL International (Hong Kong) Ltd said it would remain open but with a reduced staff to cope with express shipments expected mainly from the huge influx of visitors witnessing the historic handover.
Other smaller forwarding firms said the handover would cost them dear in lost revenue.

"I don't think anyone knows what to expect or how busy they will be because this is a unique event. We will never see anything like what's going to happen over the next few days," one freight forwarder told Reuters. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
